Subject: Re: Alert observed this morning — request for chain-of-custody evidence

Jonas / Redwood team,

We received an automated alert from our monitoring that referenced elevated geometry of API access to our account this morning at ~08:42 PT. Our security team is opening an audit and needs the following evidence to satisfy internal and external auditors (SOC 2):

- Chain-of-custody manifest for any artifacts preserved related to the event (timestamps, custodians).
- A log hash reconciliation showing that logs collected at ingestion match archived copies.
- Representative samples that demonstrate no customer payloads were exfiltrated.

Can you confirm whether any of GreenLight Bank's customer data was accessed or exported, and share the artifacts above? If you can provide an initial package today that would help us escalate appropriately.

Thanks,
Laura Kim
Senior Compliance Manager
GreenLight Bank
compliance@greenlightbank.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Chain-of-custody evidence and timeline — March 1 follow-up

Laura — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. Short answer up front: our forensic review so far indicates no customer payload was exfiltrated from production systems. Below is a concise summary plus pointers to the attached artifacts; PrIyom and Marissa are on the thread with technical and legal attestations respectively.

Summary (high level)
- Event window: 08:40:12 — 08:44:07 PT.
- Scope: transient control-plane routing anomaly affecting internal logging pipe; we observed truncated broker acknowledgements for a small subset (~0.02%) of ingestion metadata events. Customer payload stores (model inputs/outputs, embeddings) were not touched.
- Impact: metadata-only logs had partial writes to the ephemeral ingestion buffer before automatic retry; no outbound transfer or object-store delete operations were observed.

Artifacts attached to this message:
- chain_of_custody_manifest_20270301.csv  (manifest of preserved files, custodians, checksums)
- log_hashes_20270301.txt  (SHA256 hashes for sampled logs at ingestion and archived copies)
- kv_cache_samples_20270301.jsonl  (sanitized snapshots showing key families; no customer PII included)
- official_attestation_greenlight_20270301.pdf  (draft attestation for your legal/compliance team)

Forensics methods (brief)
- All preserved files were snapshotted to a sealed bucket with versioning and immutability flags set prior to analysis.
- We performed SHA256 reconciliation between live shards and the sealed archive.
- Sampling focused on sequences that overlapped the event window; samples were redacted for customer identifiers before sharing.

Next steps we propose
1) We can run an expanded, deterministic scan across the full ingestion timeframe you specify.
2) If you want a signed, notarized attestation, Marissa will finalize the PDF and route it through our legal sign-off.
3) We can schedule a 30-minute call today to walk through the artifacts; proposed time 15:00 PT.

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Laura Kim <compliance@greenlightbank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody evidence and timeline — technical notes

Laura / Jonas — adding technical detail on the log reconciliation and sampling methodology so your team can validate independently. See attached log_hashes_20270301.txt for the raw hashes.

Key points:
- Ingestion pipeline: events are written to a write-ahead queue, then to an ingest shard (S3-backed) and an index. The anomaly created a window where ACKs from the indexer to the queue were delayed; we did not observe any replication or get-object requests to external endpoints.
- Hashing: we computed SHA256 for each file at the following points: (a) post-receipt in the ingest shard, (b) after archival copy to sealed bucket, (c) on export package assembled for you. All three match for sampled files; full reconciliation report is attached.
- Sampling: deterministic sampling across sequence ids that intersect the 08:40 — 08:44 window using step=47 to avoid biased clustering. We sanitized identifiers using a one-way pseudonymization before sharing the JSONL.
- KV cache: the kv_cache_samples_20270301.jsonl contains only metadata keys and hashed identifiers; no full-text customer inputs or outputs.

Root cause (concise): a misapplied routing rule during a config rollout caused delayed ACK processing in a narrow set of ingestion shards; a subsequent fix and automated rollback restored normal ACKs. We have pushed a control-plane guardrail to prevent that rule from being applied without automated canary checks.

If GreenLight wants, we can provide the deterministic seed and sampling script so your team can reproduce the hashing locally.

—PrIyom Das
Senior Forensics Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
